absent: Full layouts of task, membership, group, subsystem state, iterator, migration context, and notifier objects beyond fields observed in fragments.
Lock ordering between group, attach, membership, signal-hand, notifier, and filesystem locks and interrupt-state rules for each helper.
Semantics of subsystem can_attach, attach, and cancel_attach hooks and meaning of the subsystem mask.
Registration, sleep, and reentrancy rules for migration and blocking notifiers and errno mapping of notifier results.
Error codes and failure behavior of destination preparation, task lookup, and per-task migration outside the shown paths.
Scheduler and freezer interaction determining when frozen tasks and stopped tasks are counted as frozen.
Timer and filesystem notification lifetime rules for event files.

findings.text: Task migration execution validates attachment per subsystem, announces default-hierarchy moves, commits task relocation, invokes per-subsystem completion hooks, then announces success and recycles the taskset for reuse.

Migration has vet, pre-notify, commit, post-notify, and cancel paths. Pre-notify failures trigger reverse-order cancellation notices followed by per-subsystem cancellation up to the failure point; after the commit point completion cannot fail and success notices omit per-task sources.

Commit moves every queued task from a source membership object to its destination object while adjusting reference and task counts, updating freezer state, and holding the membership lock across the whole relocation loop.

Membership mutation and populated-state helpers require the css_set lock held; task counting, populated checks and updates, freezer flag updates, move, and iterator advance all assert that requirement.

Tasks link into membership objects through a list node with separate active, migrating, and dying queues; membership objects carry task counts, group links, per-subsystem states, default group pointers, destination pointers, and list nodes for source and destination sets.
A membership object counts as populated when either its active or migrating queue is non-empty; transitions between empty and non-empty propagate to linked groups and per-subsystem states.

Populated accounting walks from a state toward ancestors, maintaining set and child counters plus threaded versus domain child counters, stopping when populated status is unchanged, and firing one-shot deferred offline work when a dying state becomes empty.

Emptying a group state triggers legacy release checking, populated-change tracing, and event-file notification; legacy release is scheduled only when release notification is enabled and the group is unpopulated, has no online children, and is not dead.
Online-child test walks child states under read-side critical section and reports whether any child is online, returning promptly on the first such child.

Event notification is rate limited by a minimum interval: recent notifications defer through a timer, otherwise the file node is referenced under its own lock, timestamped, and notified through the filesystem layer.

Iterator start zeroes the iterator, records subsystem and flags, selects either a subsystem-specific set list or the generic set-link list as the anchor, then advances to the first visible task under lock.

Iterator advance walks active, migrating, then dying queues within each set before moving to the next set; removal of the current task is tolerated through a skipped marker that suppresses one position step.

Iteration hides exiting tasks with no live signal members unless an explicit with-dead option is set; process mode further restricts results to group leaders and hides dying leaders without live members, while task mode skips all dying entries.

Legacy transfer drains all tasks from one group to another one task at a time, skipping exiting tasks, holding global attach and group locks, registering all current sets as sources, preparing destinations, and finishing the migration context on all paths.

Destination vetting accepts all legacy destinations; default-hierarchy destinations must be valid domains, with thread roots and threaded groups exempt and groups with enabled controllers rejected when they would violate the no-internal-process rule.

Thread eligibility distinguishes mixable roots, thread roots, threaded groups, and domains: only the hierarchy root is mixable, threaded groups cannot host domains, thread roots are domains with threaded children or with tasks plus threaded controllers, and mixability exempts ancestor checks.
Blocking notification checks for subscribers with an unsynchronized read, then takes the head read lock and walks the chain; absence of subscribers yields a done result without locking.

Chain walk follows next pointers with raw dereference, optionally validates handler addresses in debug builds, traces each handler, counts invocations, and stops when a handler returns a stop indication or when a call budget is exhausted.
Robust chain walk issues an up notification to all handlers and, only when stopped, issues a compensating down notification limited to the handlers already invoked.

Freezer migration ignores kernel threads, takes a fast path when neither endpoint requests freezing and the task is unfrozen, otherwise transfers frozen-task accounting, refreshes frozen status on both endpoints, and forces the task toward the destination freeze request.
A group is frozen when freezing is requested and its frozen-task count equals its total task count; total task count is the sum over linked membership task counts.

Frozen-flag changes notify the event file and trace the transition, then propagate upward: freezing accumulates frozen descendants and continues only through freezing ancestors whose descendants are all frozen, while unfreezing decrements ancestors unconditionally.

Per-task freeze control takes the task signal-hand lock and returns silently if the task is exiting; it sets or clears a freeze trap and wakes the task, using a signal wake when freezing and a direct wake when thawing.
Kernel-text validation dereferences possible function descriptors with fault-tolerant load, then accepts core kernel text, including init text before init memory is freed, or module text.
Subsystem-mask iteration degenerates to a single no-subsystem pass when subsystem configuration support is absent; otherwise it visits each set bit and resolves the corresponding subsystem object.

Moving a task expects a non-empty membership link when a source exists and an empty link when there is no source, warns on violation, and must not observe the exiting flag because exit paths can concurrently release the membership object.
Frozen-task decrement warns if the counter becomes negative, indicating unbalanced frozen accounting across migration or state changes.
Task and freezer control uses exiting and kernel-thread task flags, a freeze-trap job control flag, and group freeze-request and frozen-state flags.
Migration and notification protocol uses migrating, migrated, and canceled migration events plus done and stop-mask notifier results.
Task iteration mode uses flags for skipped position, process-only versus all tasks, and inclusion of dead tasks.
